title: Refraction ray diagram sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 22 (Refraction ray diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 22: Refraction. To understand how light changes speed and direction when it passes between materials

picture.alt: A ray bending through a glass block
picture.draw: Draw and label: Refraction ray diagram sheet

questions.q: Light leaves glass into air at an angle. Which way does it bend?
questions.a: Away from the normal (it speeds up).
questions.model: New medium: air, less dense than glass. Light speeds up. Speeding up bends it away from the normal.

questions.q: Why does a ray along the normal not bend?
questions.a: It meets the boundary head on, so all of the wavefront changes speed at once.

questions.q: How many times faster is light in air than in glass (chart)?
Core: Try the disappearing coin and the bent straw at home. Draw ray diagrams explaining each.
questions.a: Rays bend away from the normal leaving the water, so objects appear higher; diagrams show this.
questions.model: Teacher draws the coin first: ray from coin to water surface, bending away from the normal towards the eye; dashed line back shows where the coin appears.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why a swimming pool looks shallower than it really is (portal response box).
questions.a: Light from the bottom bends away from the normal at the surface; we trace rays back in straight lines, so the bottom appears higher.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain refraction with the 'marching soldiers' model.
questions.a: When one side of a row reaches slower ground first it slows, so the row turns towards the normal.

questions.q: Light slows down entering glass and bends...
Big question: why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
questions.a: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water, so the underwater part appears in a different place.
